chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'What the hunting dogs kill, provided you have mentioned the name of Allah upon it, then eat from their catch; and what the dogs kill that you did not train, before you reach it, then do not eat it.'

key_terms.ذَكَرْتُمُ اسْمَ اللَّهِ: you mentioned the name of Allah (reciting Bismillah)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for eating game caught by hunting dogs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam al-Baqir from Imam Ali, establishes the critical condition of *tasmiyah* (reciting Allah's name) at the moment of sending the trained hunting dog, linking the permissibility of the meat directly to the hunter's mindfulness of God. It further clarifies the ruling for untrained dogs by noting that their catch is invalid because they do not consume it in the manner of a deliberate sacrifice but rather as scavengers, a distinction emphasized in Shia jurisprudence regarding the purity of game. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of hunting within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, illustrating the practical application of Quranic verses on lawful game.
